1970.notes: Pre-1971 income tax: 30 Del. C. 1953 sec. 1111 as amended by 51 Del. Laws c. 299 (effective Jan. 1, 1957: 1.5%-8%, top bracket over $8,000) and 53 Del. Laws c. 104 (1961, https://legis.delaware.gov/SessionLaws/Chapter?id=30084), which added 9% ($30,000-$50,000), 10% ($50,000-$100,000) and 11% (over $100,000); no further rate amendment appears in the 54th-57th volumes of Delaware Laws before the Personal Income Tax Law of 1970 (57 Del. Laws c. 737, effective 1971) re-enacted the same schedule. Applied to net income after exemptions; same schedule for all filing statuses. Deduction not recorded: pre-1971 personal exemption / dependent credit amounts not verified (standard deduction was the lesser of 10% of AGI or $500, $1,000 joint, per 55 Del. Laws c. 363). Federal income tax paid deductible up to $300 ($600 joint) - not modelled.

1971.notes: Schedule of the Personal Income Tax Law of 1970 (57 Del. Laws c 737, effective 1971); the 2-3k bracket rate is garbled in the online text and read as 3% (consistent with 3.3% = +10% in 59 Del. Laws c 152). 58 Del. Laws c 300 raised rates above $8,000 (to 8.5%-18% above $20,000) for income earned Aug 1 - Dec 31, 1971 - that proration is NOT modelled. Same schedule for all filing statuses. Standard deduction was 10% of AGI up to $1,000 ($500 married separate) - income-dependent, not modelled; deduction = $600 personal exemption(s) only. Federal income tax paid was deductible (capped; repealed 1988) - not modelled.
